application.outputs: The pallet pose (position and yaw of the pallet face in the camera RGB optical frame). The pallet width, height, and depth in metres. Which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. The handling process uses those results while the scene can still change, so the result must stay within the protected latency budget of 5 ms.
application.purpose: pps is the pallet perception stack on an AGV. It detects pallets in a scene that can still change and estimates a pose the vehicle can use for dynamic handling. Stage 1 is the RT-DETR detector, which publishes 2D pallet detections. Stage 2 is the chamfer geometry pipeline in geometry_core (estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2), wrapped by pallet_pose_cpp_node: it synchronizes those detections with a depth image and estimates the pallet face pose in the camera RGB optical frame.
application.users: The vehicle's dynamic handling process. It needs a pallet pose while the scene can still change, so it can approach and handle the pallet. The rich PalletPoseStamped message is the pose result intended for that AGV controller.

rejected_features.summary: Publish the pallet face width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped. Width and height are the spans of the plane inliers already built inside estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, along that estimate's plane axes. Depth is the mean z of those same inliers after the depth-to-RGB transform that already places the face centre. The handling process can then size the approach from this synchronized capture while the scene can still change.

For each stage-2 estimate, build the chamfer prototype from the width and height of the pallet face already recovered as plane inliers in that depth frame, instead of the fixed 1.20 m by 0.14 m factory face, so the template is the pallet the vehicle is about to handle.

For the detections in one capture, return which pallets are sent through stage 2 and which are deferred. select_stage2_subset ranks the existing DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements, admits at most the count this capture will pose, and places every remaining candidate in deferred. Stage2Admission holds those two vectors, admitted and deferred, and each candidate keeps its source_index. The pose node calls it with its detection_selection strategy and a count of one, so stage 2 still estimates that single admitted pallet, and the other candidates in this array stay on the deferred vector for this capture. An empty candidate list returns both vectors empty, and an unknown strategy throws. The count is set for this capture because the scene can still change and stage 2 poses a subset of the array.

For each synchronized detection and depth pair, send stage 2 the two class-matched pallet faces with the largest area_px, breaking remaining ties by higher score and then by lower source index, and mark every other candidate deferred. Each admitted face is passed to estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, and each success publishes its own PalletPoseStamped from that capture. Each deferred candidate is published as its source index together with this pair's RGB and depth stamps. A pair with fewer than two candidates admits every candidate and defers none. The handling process then has the poses of the large faces in this capture and the identities of the detections this pair did not pose, while the scene can still change.
